title: Scale Model Builder
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Geometry
description: Pick a real object and a scale, then see how the lengths, floor area, and volume of the scale model compare with the original.

educational.topic: Scale factor and its effect on length, area, and volume
learningObjectives: Students will be able to apply a scale factor to find the dimensions of a scale model and analyze how the scale affects length, area, and volume.
prerequisites: Area and volume of a rectangular prism

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Real-world modeling with familiar size references
keyQuestions: Why does the volume shrink so much faster than the length?
If a model uses 200 cm² of card for the floor at 1:50, how much floor does the real building have?
Which scale would you choose for a model of a basketball court, and why?
commonMisconceptions: Area and volume scale by the same factor as length.
A 1:10 model uses one tenth of the material (it has one thousandth of the volume).
A larger k means a larger model.
assessmentOpportunities: A model car is 18 cm long and the real car is 4.5 m long. Students find the scale, then determine how many times greater the real car's volume is than the model's.
